audit_findings.title: Recurring franchise-acquisition cash outlays may be missing from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $83.4 million in 2025; 30.3% of the $275.3 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring franchise-agreement acquisition cash payments reduce owner earnings or must be funded within the forecast growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, the Company's net franchise agreement acquisition costs were $83.4 million, $112.2 million, and $98.3 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The payments are demonstrated recurring cash outlays, but the supplied valuation does not show whether they remain in the owner-earnings calculation. Omitting the 2025 amount would materially inflate the anchor and every scenario.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $275.3 million anchor line by line to the cash-flow statement and rerun all scenarios if the full $83.4 million net payment was not deducted.

audit_findings.title: The stakes bridge may re-add operating development capital already represented in earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $220.7 million bridge addition, equal to $4.75 per diluted share and 5.3% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The stakes addition affects the equity bridge, while affiliate income, losses, distributions and growth-related capital requirements affect owner earnings and forecast reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has equity method investments in affiliates primarily related to the Company's program to offer equity support to qualified franchisees to develop and operate Cambria Hotels and Everhome Suites in strategic markets.
audit_findings.explanation: The affiliates are demonstrably connected to hotel development, but the record does not identify the assets included in stakes_net or establish consistent removal of their results from owner earnings. Excluding an operating stake could reduce value by up to $4.75 per share before correcting any retained affiliate losses; purging those losses could offset part of that reduction. The bridge correction could move the $103.99 bull value below the $100.62 market price.
audit_findings.action: Inventory every component of stakes_net, classify detachable versus growth-required capital, purge the corresponding affiliate results from OE, and rerun the bridge and scenarios consistently.

audit_findings.title: Unrecorded guarantees are contingent claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $40.4 million latest limited-payment principal exposure plus $18.2 million management-arrangement exposure; $58.6 million combined, or $1.26 per share and 1.4% of base equity value, excluding unquantified expenses and interest
audit_findings.mechanism: Expected guarantee payments would reduce the equity bridge or future owner earnings when incurred.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the maximum unrecorded exposure of the principal associated with these limited payment guaranties was $38.5 million, plus unpaid expenses and accrued but unpaid interest.
audit_findings.explanation: The claims are real contingencies, but no payment obligation is presently demonstrated and the company assesses the limited-payment guarantees as remote. Even deducting the full $58.6 million known maximum would reduce base value from $89.00 to about $87.74 and bull value from $103.99 to about $102.73, leaving the stated valuation conclusions unchanged. Unpaid expenses and interest remain unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Maintain a current guarantee schedule, obtain probability and recourse assessments, and revisit the bridge if expected losses, accrued interest or expenses become measurable.

audit_findings.title: Reimbursable operations have produced recurring deficits rather than breaking even
audit_findings.magnitude: $47.1 million in 2025, equal to 17.1% of the anchor; $72.2 million in the first six months of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Any stripped deficit or overstated recovery asset raises owner earnings; persistent deficits may also require a lower sustainable OE anchor or growth assumption.
audit_findings.evidence: During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, reimbursable expenses from franchised and managed properties exceeded revenue for reimbursable costs from franchised and managed properties by $47.1 million, $18.2 million, and $32.8 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The deficits are demonstrated and have accelerated in 2026. They remain expenses under GAAP, but the supplied valuation does not show whether the OE pipeline retained them or assumed complete recovery. Removing the 2025 deficit would materially overstate the anchor, while the 2026 amount raises a separate sustainability concern.
audit_findings.action: Trace reimbursable revenue, expenses and related working-capital movements into each OE year; inspect advance balances, aging and subsequent collections; rerun the anchor and growth cases for any excluded or uncollectible amount.

audit_findings.title: The PVRSU share ceiling may not be a true maximum
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to 0.550471 million incremental shares if the 0.423439 million inventory is at target and all awards reach 230%; 1.2% of the 46.421453 million denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: Additional PVRSU vesting increases the fully diluted share denominator and reduces per-share value.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company granted PVRSUs with performance conditions, PVRSUs with market conditions, and PVRSUs with performance and market conditions, with requisite service periods between 9 months and 48 months and with award vesting ranges generally between 0 % and 230 % of the initial units granted.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the reported inventory is target or maximum remains unresolved, but the filed general payout ceiling supplies a conservative scale. Adding the computed 0.550471 million shares would reduce base value from $89.00 to about $87.96 and bull value from $103.99 to about $102.77, which does not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $100.62 price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the reporting basis and contractual maximum for each outstanding PVRSU tranche, then update the ceiling denominator; no operating-value rerun is needed unless awards permit more than the disclosed general ceiling.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor spans a mid-year step acquisition despite a null perimeter ruling
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed $1.318 million reduction between reported 2025 net income excluding the $100.025 million gain ($269.921 million) and filed full-year pro forma net income ($268.603 million), equal to 0.5% of the $275.3 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: A full-year pro forma perimeter can alter the 2025 OE anchor and historical growth comparability through operating earnings, incremental interest, amortization and capital needs.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company's consolidated statements of income include Choice Hotels Canada's results of operations since the July 2, 2025 acquisition date.
audit_findings.explanation: The mixed ownership perimeter is demonstrated, but the filed full-year pro forma results indicate only a $1.318 million net-income normalization after removing the remeasurement gain. That scale is insufficient to change the valuation conclusion, although the exact owner-earnings adjustment is unquantified and could be positive or negative because cash adjustments differ from net income.
audit_findings.action: Document removal of the $100.025 million gain and calculate a full-year pro forma 2025 OE reconciliation, including interest, amortization and capital outlays, to close the perimeter record.
